risks.note: Order flow is tied to large public-sector and terminal projects and is described as lumpy; deferrals or tender-cycle changes can shift revenue between periods even when the underlying structural demand trend is intact.

Exposure to price fluctuation in basic raw materials such as steel, components and power, as well as in finished goods used in manufacturing; management relies on customer relationships and value-added product mix to mitigate, rather than hedging.

Currency-market volatility can affect overall profitability, and rupee depreciation raises the landed cost of imported components and instruments, pressuring margins where input costs cannot be fully passed through.

Any increase in interest rates can affect finance cost; the Company currently manages this via minimal dependence on debt, but flags rights-issue fundraising as its stated fallback if funds are needed.

risks.risk: Customer capex risk from energy-price/supply shocks
risks.note: A renewed spike in crude prices (2026 reference forecast already about 21% above the 2025 average) or an adverse scenario of oil 80-100% above baseline could compress global growth and delay discretionary capital expenditure by the Company's energy-sector customers.

risks.risk: Higher financing costs affecting customer investment decisions
risks.note: Rising long-term financing costs disproportionately affect capital-intensive energy projects in emerging economies and could slow final investment decisions on terminals and pipelines that generate the Company's order flow.

risks.risk: Fiscal strain on public-sector customers from fuel under-recoveries
risks.note: State-owned refiners incurred losses of Rs 74,781 crore in the April-June 2026 quarter as retail prices were held; this fiscal burden could defer discretionary PSU capital expenditure, a key source of the Company's domestic order pipeline.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Designs and manufactures metering, filtration, dosing and fluid-handling equipment for the point of measurement and transfer in oil, gas and chemical logistics, serving public-sector oil marketing companies and global automation/instrumentation leaders from an integrated Vadodara facility.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Cryogenic OGS designs and manufactures metering, filtration, dosing and fluid-handling equipment for the oil and gas, chemical and allied industries, focused on the critical point where fuel or gas is measured, loaded or transferred (terminals, truck/wagon loading bays, LNG last-mile distribution). It is making a deliberate strategic shift from supplying engineering and assembly components to delivering complete turnkey solutions by procuring and integrating every key component of a project. Products span custody-transfer metering skids, LNG/cryogenic metering and loading skids, filtration and air-separation equipment, additive dosing systems, calibration/proving equipment, density instrumentation, specialty lifting jigs for wind turbines, and ASME-code pressure vessels and piping spools.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Core: Metering skids (custody transfer), Air eliminators, Basket strainers (80-90% market share in catalog items for PSUs). New: aDENS Density Probe (import substitute, 3-4 initial orders). Diversification: Nacelle lifting jigs for Suzlon (Wind energy).

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Measurement & Custody Transfer Solutions:** Metering Skids for Liquids (MS/HSD/SKO), Custody Transfer Systems, LNG Metering and Truck/Wagon Loading Skids, Hydrogen and Green Ammonia Metering Skids, Natural Gas Metering Skids, Truck and Wagon Loading/Unloading Skids (Liquids), ATF Metering & Filtration Skids, Pressure Reduction Skids
- **Filtration & Air Separation Solutions:** Basket Strainers, Duplex Basket Strainers, Air Eliminators, Strainer Cum Air (Vapor) Eliminators
- **Fuel Conditioning & Additive Injection Solutions:** Additive Dosing Systems, Additive Injection Panels, Chemical Dosing Skids
- **Process Instrumentation & Quality Monitoring Solutions:** aDENS Density Measurement System, Density Probes, Inline Density Monitoring Systems
- **Calibration & Verification Solutions:** Prover Tanks, Calibration Tanks, Master Meter Trolleys, Calibration Skids
- **Engineered Process & Turnkey Solutions:** Design and Engineering Services, Custom Process Skids, Modular Process Packages, Turnkey Engineering Solutions, Custom Fabrication, ASME-code Pressure Vessels and Piping Spools
- **Specialty Lifting and Handling Solutions:** Nacelle Lifting Jigs

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: 22-25 Crores (confirmed post-sales); 65 Crores (bids submitted); Key projects include 143 truck loading skids for Egypt (Emerson) and custody transfer skid for Honeywell Nigeria.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: Expect similar H2FY26 growth as H1 (implied ~50%+ full year); Margin: Aim to maintain ~30% EBITDA, potential upside from international mix; Order Inflow: Aggressive pursuit of LNG and international projects; Capex: New facility planning initiated, expected need in 2-3 years at 75-100 Cr revenue threshold.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: 1) Transition to full turnkey model (procuring high-value valves/meters) increasing ticket size and value add. 2) aDENS density probe replacing European imports in tank farms. 3) International expansion (Middle East/Africa) with better margins. 4) LNG and Green Hydrogen metering technologies.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's gas infrastructure build-out (raising gas's share of the primary energy mix from about 6.7% to 15% by 2030, demand growing nearly 60% to 297 mmscmd, 10,805 km of pipeline expansion) requires metering, filtration and pressure regulation at every geographical area, pipeline kilometre and CNG station
- The LNG cycle, domestic and global: eight Indian terminals with 52.7 MMTPA of regasification capacity being supplemented by new land-based and floating units, LNG imports up 15.4% in FY26, and 2026-2028 bringing record additions to global LNG export capacity, each requiring custody transfer metering, prover tanks, filtration, dosing and pressure reduction skids over a multi-year cycle
- Refining and petrochemical expansion (India refining capacity growth from 258.1 to 309.5 MMTPA by 2030, alongside large exploration & production and petrochemical capital programmes) sustaining demand for metering skids, additive dosing and calibration infrastructure
- Wind energy at home and in export markets: record wind capacity additions in India and globally expanding the market for nacelle lifting jigs and installation tooling, with an export corridor opening in Middle East onshore wind
- Green hydrogen readiness under the National Green Hydrogen Mission establishing long-cycle demand for ultra-precise flow measurement, pressure regulation and gas purity management
- Rising instrumentation content per site as compressed-biogas blending increases (1% in FY26 rising to 5% from FY29), making gas composition more variable and favouring density instrumentation and intelligent measurement over commodity hardware
- Threats flagged: renewed energy-supply disruption/high crude prices delaying discretionary capex; domestic inflation and weak rural demand; higher financing costs slowing final investment decisions on terminals/pipelines; fiscal strain on state-owned refiners from fuel under-recoveries deferring PSU capex; slower global trade and costlier logistics weighing on export competitiveness; rupee depreciation raising landed cost of imported components; lumpy order flow tied to large public-sector/terminal projects creating project timing and concentration risk
- Secured multiple orders for LNG truck loading skids during the year and continued supplying metering and loading systems to petroleum terminals
- Received a direct purchase order from Honeywell LNG LLC, USA, described as reaffirming the Company's growing credibility in global energy infrastructure markets in its first year as a listed entity
- Order for 143 truck loading skids for an Egypt-based end user, contracted through an EPC contractor, cited as one of the Company's largest to date
- Libya and Nigeria project references and ADNOC enlistment cited as building the reference base for the next tier of export tenders
- Infravolt Engineering's (51%-owned) first two orders, worth ₹17.85 crore, secured within weeks of incorporation in early FY27

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margins ~30% sustained despite higher pass-through costs in turnkey model due to: 1) Better procurement pricing vs MNCs. 2) Value capture in design/engineering selection. 3) Higher margin profile of international projects vs domestic.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Zero-debt balance sheet. IPO proceeds and operating cash (27 Cr cash on hand) allocated to working capital for turnkey procurement (valves/meters) and gradual new facility development.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company's integrated manufacturing and assembly facility at Por Industrial Park, Vadodara spans roughly 9,300 square meters on a 30-year long-term facility lease, bringing design, assembly and testing together under one roof. During FY2025-26 the Company acquired additional expansion land amounting to 4x the existing facility area for future capacity, alongside continued investment in the manufacturing base to support larger opportunities. The facility carries concurrent production capacity for 200 skids and ran at 45% average capacity utilisation in FY2025-26, giving headroom before the expansion land needs to be built out. Separately, the Company advanced its proprietary aDENS density probe (developed with a European partner) towards commercialisation during the year.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and aggressive on growth; emphasizing 'financial discipline' and 'zero debt' while pivoting business model. Transparent about capacity constraints and future capex needs.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- 90%+ repeat-customer rate across 300+ installation locations/terminals served
- Fully integrated single-site facility (design, assembly, hydrostatic/pneumatic testing, NDE, wiring, factory acceptance testing all in-house) giving control over quality and project timelines rather than depending on client-supplied items
- Regulatory/qualification barriers to entry held by the company: EIL pre-qualification (described in the MD&A as 'a formidable barrier to entry' for competitors), ASME U-Stamp, ADNOC vendor enlistment
- Proprietary aDENS resonant-vibration density probe developed with a European partner for real-time in-line liquid density measurement
- Reference customer base with global instrumentation OEMs (ABB, Honeywell, Emerson, Endress+Hauser) and marquee deliveries (Konkan LNG, Petronet LNG, Honeywell LNG USA, Honeywell Nigeria) that the company cites as building credibility for larger tenders
- Debt-free balance sheet; growth funded from internal accruals and IPO proceeds rather than borrowed capital

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: 1) Customer Concentration: Top 10 customers = 89% of revenue (dependent on EPC spend by IOCL/BPCL). 2) Execution Risk: Scaling turnkey model requires working capital management. 3) Raw Material/Component dependency on imports for high-end instruments.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: The company holds an 80-90% market share in specific catalog items (air eliminators/strainers) across 200+ PSU terminals, creating a massive installed base for 10-year replacement cycles. The 'aDENS' probe approval is in Cryogenic's name, legally blocking the European tech partner from direct entry into India.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Move from supplying components toward delivering complete, integrated (turnkey) solutions
- Convert hard-won approvals (EIL vendor status, ADNOC enlistment, ASME U-Stamp) into actual projects, at home and in the Gulf
- Extend precision manufacturing into components the energy transition will need (wind, solar, railway power electronics via Infravolt, green hydrogen readiness)
- Diversify beyond oil-and-gas equipment via the 51%-owned Infravolt Engineering entity to reduce single-sector dependence, applying the same precision fabrication and quality-system discipline to an adjacent components …
